subject: Quantara pilot: request for temporary latency penalty waiver & alternate remedies
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Park <alan@quantara.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot SLOs — proposed temporary adjustment and remedies

Hi Alan,

Great to see Quantara commit to the 12-week pilot. A couple of items came up from our engineering side as we map the workload to hosted capacity and I wanted to propose a pragmatic approach so we can ship the pilot without delaying the start date.

Ask (summary):
- Temporarily lower the uptime SLO for the pilot from 99.95% to 99.5% (pilot window: Aug 9 — Oct 1).
- Waive standard latency-based service credits for latency tiers tied to production-scale QPS during the pilot (Quantara will remain on a discounted rate for pilot).

Why this helps:
- Quantara will be running a bespoke synthetic workload and extended KV cache invalidation as part of evaluation; forecasting shows a nontrivial risk of transient latency spikes that are unlikely to be representative of full production.
- Our standard credits would be large and punitive for a short pilot, which will make the commercial economics untenable given the pilot discount.

What Redwood will commit to in lieu of credits:
- Dedicated on-call for pilot hours (Mon–Fri 6am–10pm PT) and escalation to SRE lead within 30m for incidents impacting experiment completion.
- Weekly health reports with latency percentiles and token-cost breakdowns.
- A non-refundable $10k operational credit toward a dedicated reservation if Quantara converts to Dedicated within 60 days of pilot close.

Attached: pilot-matrix and our suggested SLA redline v2 for the pilot period.

If this is acceptable to you we'll need exec sign-off on the commercial carveout and legal to accept the pilot redline. Would you prefer we route through your procurement first or work with your engineering PO?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference

Priyom,

Thanks — this looks reasonable and I appreciate the detail. A couple of clarifications from our side before I push to procurement:

- Pilot must still guarantee a maximum 1-hour P0 response and we need telemetry access so our ML team can ingest p95/p99 latencies. Can you confirm the health report schema and that we can pull a read-only view of the dashboard?
- The operational credit toward a Dedicated reservation is appealing, but procurement will want a firm dollar cap on waived credits during the pilot — can Redwood confirm a maximum exposure number for the pilot period if we proceed without standard credits?

If we can confirm those two items I will route to procurement and legal. Our internal target is to have the pilot signed off by Aug 6 to start Aug 9.

— Alan

Team — forwarding the thread (see below). Quantara wants two confirmations before procurement signs:

1) Telemetry access: they need a read-only dashboard extract (p95/p99 + per-route token counts) that their ML team can ingest. This is standard — engineering says we can provide a signed, time-limited tokenized export for the pilot.

2) A hard cap on Redwood's exposure if we waive latency credits during the pilot. Finance asks for a maximum liability number so this can go into the deal desk record. Based on the pilot profile and the discounted unit price, my estimate of worst-case credit exposure over the 12-week window is $22,500 if we left credit policy fully in place. If we waive credits, I'd recommend we cap exposure at $25k and compensate with the operational commitments below.

Proposed internal approval request (what I'm asking from you):
- Executive sign-off to temporarily waive latency-triggered service credits for the pilot in exchange for: 1) 99.5% uptime SLO for pilot window (Aug 9—Oct 1); 2) dedicated on-call and weekly health reports; 3) $10k conversion credit toward Dedicated reservation; 4) cap Redwood exposure at $25k.
- Authority to instruct Legal to accept the pilot redline (attached) and to record the cap in the Deal Desk notes.
- If you prefer a smaller cap, suggest a number — finance/ops needs one before we pass to procurement.

Why I think this is acceptable: the pilot is strategic (Quantara is a sizable potential customer for our multi-region Dedicated product), the discount is aggressive and the credit exposure window is short. The alternate remedies materially reduce operational risk for the customer without creating open-ended financial liability for Redwood.

Please reply with APPROVE / REJECT / MODIFY and any preferred cap. If APPROVE, cc Legal (Lauren Bishop) and Finance (Ben Carter) and I'll shepherd the redline through.

Thanks,
